title: AVD Anywhere
subtitle: Azure Virtual Desktop on Azure, Azure Local, and AVD Hybrid Platforms
followAlongPolicy: Full follow-along: every demo has an attendee version. Azure and the portability pattern need no special hardware; Azure Local and Hybrid steps are hypervisor-agnostic with lab values as variables.

variables.name: <rg>
variables.meaning: your resource group for the AVD control plane

variables.name: <location>
variables.meaning: an Azure region, for example eastus

variables.name: <user>
variables.meaning: a cloud-only test user, for example user1@yourtenant.onmicrosoft.com

variables.name: <storageaccount>
variables.meaning: a globally unique storage account name for the profile share

variables.name: <profile-share>
variables.meaning: the Azure Files share that holds the profile containers

variables.name: <odfc-share>
variables.meaning: the Azure Files share that holds the Office containers

demos.title: One workspace, three host pools, all Available

followAlong.goal: See your own workspace, host pools and session host status in one view.
needs: An AVD workspace with at least one host pool
Az.DesktopVirtualization module

steps.title: List host pools in the workspace's resource group
steps.instructions: List the host pools and the status of their session hosts.
steps.command:
Get-AzWvdHostPool -ResourceGroupName <rg> | Select-Object Name, HostPoolType, LoadBalancerType
Get-AzWvdHostPool -ResourceGroupName <rg> | ForEach-Object { Get-AzWvdSessionHost -ResourceGroupName <rg> -HostPoolName $_.Name | Select-Object Name, Status, Session }
steps.check: Each host pool lists its session hosts with Status Available.

troubleshooting: Status Unavailable: check the host's network access to the AVD service URLs and the agent version.

followAlong.goal: Understand how the foundation is organised so you can adapt it.
needs: The repo checked out

steps.title: Read the solution layout
steps.instructions: Open automation/landing-zones/avd and compare the Bicep and Terraform folders; both take the inputs listed in solution.yml.
steps.check: You can find bicep/, terraform/ and solution.yml.

steps.title: Run a what-if of the foundation against your subscription
steps.instructions: Copy the example parameter file, replace the values with yours, and run a what-if. Nothing is created.
steps.command: az deployment sub what-if --location <location> --template-file automation/landing-zones/avd/bicep/main.bicep --parameters <your parameter file>
steps.check: A list of resources that would be created; no errors.

troubleshooting: Provider not registered: register Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization first.

followAlong.goal: Enable Entra Kerberos on an Azure Files share and confirm a Windows 11 Entra-joined VM obtains a ticket.
needs: An Entra-joined Windows 11 VM
A storage account (FileStorage or StorageV2) with a file share
Rights to grant admin consent
Note: cloud-only identity support is a preview feature

steps.title: Enable Entra Kerberos on the storage account
steps.instructions: In the portal: Storage account > File shares > Identity-based access > Microsoft Entra Kerberos > Set up. Enable it, then grant admin consent to the generated app registration.
steps.check: An app named [Storage Account] <storageaccount>.file.core.windows.net exists with consent granted.

steps.title: Allow the ticket to be issued without MFA
steps.instructions: Exclude the storage account's app from Conditional Access policies that require MFA; the ticket request is silent and cannot prompt.
steps.check: The app appears under Exclude in the policy.

steps.title: Enable cloud-only group support
steps.instructions: In the app registration manifest add the tag kdc_enable_cloud_group_sids. Use security groups that are not nested.
steps.check: The tag appears in the manifest tags array.

steps.title: Enable ticket retrieval on the client
steps.instructions: Set the registry value that lets the client request the Entra Kerberos ticket and restart the client.
steps.check: Value is 1.

steps.title: Assign share-level permission
steps.instructions: Assign Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor to your users group on the share.
steps.command: New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <group object id> -RoleDefinitionName 'Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor' -Scope <share resource id>
steps.check: The role assignment lists on the share.

steps.title: Request the ticket
steps.instructions: Restart the client, then sign in again to the VM as an Entra user (the registry value takes effect at sign-in) and request a ticket for the storage account.
steps.check: klist shows a ticket for the cifs service of the storage account.

troubleshooting: No ticket: check the client is Entra-joined or hybrid-joined, the registry value, and the MFA exclusion.
Access denied after the ticket: check the share-level role and the NTFS ACL.
cleanup: Remove the role assignment and disable Entra Kerberos on the storage account if it was a test.

demos.title: AVD on Azure: host pool and session hosts

followAlong.goal: Create a pooled host pool, desktop application group and workspace.
needs: Az.DesktopVirtualization
Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization provider registered
A resource group

steps.title: Create the host pool
steps.instructions: Create a pooled, breadth-first host pool with a session limit.
steps.check: Get-AzWvdHostPool returns hp-demo-azure.

steps.title: Create the desktop application group
steps.instructions: Create a desktop application group for the pool.
steps.check: The application group lists the host pool.

steps.title: Create the workspace and register the group
steps.instructions: Create the workspace and add the application group.
steps.check: The workspace lists the application group.

steps.title: Entitle a user group
steps.instructions: Assign the Desktop Virtualization User role on the application group.
steps.check: The users appear on the application group's assignments.

cleanup: Remove the workspace, application group and host pool when finished.

demos.title: One image artifact: Image Builder to gallery to host pool

followAlong.goal: Build a Windows 11 multi-session image with Azure Image Builder into a Compute Gallery.
needs: Compute Gallery with an image definition
Image Builder identity with the gallery roles
Microsoft.VirtualMachineImages provider registered

steps.title: Resolve an exact source image version
steps.instructions: Pin an exact marketplace version for reproducibility (Image Builder also accepts latest, resolved at build time).
steps.check: An exact version number is returned.

steps.title: Deploy the template
steps.instructions: Deploy the Image Builder template from the repo with your gallery and identity.
steps.command: az deployment group create -g <rg> --template-file automation/avd/images/azure/bicep/main.bicep --parameters <your parameter file>
steps.check: The template shows provisioning Succeeded.

steps.title: Start the build
steps.instructions: Start the build; it takes 45 to 90 minutes.
steps.check: Run state moves to Running, then Succeeded.

steps.title: Confirm the gallery image version
steps.instructions: List the versions of the image definition.
steps.check: A new version with ProvisioningState Succeeded.

troubleshooting: Build fails at the customiser: open the staging resource group's customization log.
cleanup: Delete the image template and old image versions to avoid storage cost.

followAlong.goal: Enable AVD Insights for a host pool.
needs: A Log Analytics workspace
Session hosts with Azure Monitor Agent

steps.title: Open Insights and run the configuration workbook
steps.instructions: In the portal open Azure Virtual Desktop > Insights, select the subscription, and use Open configuration workbook.
steps.check: The configuration workbook reports diagnostics enabled for the host pool and workspace.

steps.title: Associate the Insights data collection rule with the hosts
steps.instructions: Create the data collection rule from the workbook and associate it with the session hosts.
steps.check: Host performance counters and events appear after the first collection interval.

troubleshooting: No data: allow time for the first collection; confirm the Azure Monitor Agent is installed.
cleanup: Delete the data collection rule and association if it was a test.

demos.title: Data collection rules that keep costs sane

followAlong.goal: Measure what your session hosts cost to monitor and keep only what you need.
needs: A Log Analytics workspace with host data

steps.title: Measure ingestion by table
steps.instructions: Run the query in your workspace.
steps.command: Usage | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where IsBillable == true | summarize GB = sum(Quantity)/1000.0 by DataType | order by GB desc
steps.check: A ranked list of tables by billable GB.

steps.title: Review the DCR data sources
steps.instructions: Open the data collection rule and review counters, sampling rates and event channels; remove what you do not use.
steps.check: Only the counters and channels that Insights and your alerts need remain.

demos.title: AVD on Azure Local: host pool and a session host as an Azure Local VM

followAlong.goal: Understand how an Azure Local VM becomes an AVD session host; the steps need an Azure Local cluster.
needs: An Azure Local cluster with an Arc Resource Bridge and a custom location (not required to read)

steps.title: Create the VM from Azure
steps.instructions: Create an Azure Local VM from a gallery image on a logical network, then register it to the host pool with a registration token passed in memory.
steps.command: az stack-hci-vm create --name <vm> --resource-group <rg> --custom-location <custom location id> --image <image name> --admin-username <admin> --admin-password <read from a secure prompt, never typed into a script> --nics <nic name> --storage-path-id <storage path id>
steps.check: The VM lists as Succeeded under Azure Local virtual machines.

steps.title: Register to the host pool
steps.instructions: Run the registration step with a token generated at deploy time.
steps.check: The host appears Available in the pool.

troubleshooting: Host Unavailable: check outbound access to the AVD service URLs from the logical network.
cleanup: Delete the VM and remove the session host from the pool.

demos.title: GPU on Azure Local: assignment mode and evidence
Plain Hyper-V VMs seen in Azure only as Arc machines

followAlong.goal: Make an ordinary Windows VM on any hypervisor an Arc-enabled server.
needs: A Windows 11 Enterprise VM (any hypervisor)
Rights to onboard Arc machines (Azure Connected Machine Onboarding on the resource group)
Outbound access to the Arc endpoints

steps.title: Create the onboarding principal
steps.instructions: Create a service principal scoped only to the Arc resource group.
steps.command:
$sp = New-AzADServicePrincipal -DisplayName spn-arc-onboard
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $sp.Id -RoleDefinitionName 'Azure Connected Machine Onboarding' -Scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<arc rg>
steps.check: The role assignment exists on the Arc resource group.

steps.title: Install and connect the Connected Machine agent in the guest
steps.instructions: In the guest, in an elevated session, download and run AzureConnectedMachineAgent.msi from the Microsoft download link in the Azure Arc documentation, then run the onboarding. Pass the secret in memory and never store it.
steps.check: azcmagent show reports Connected.

troubleshooting: Agent cannot connect: check outbound access to the Arc endpoints and the system clock.
cleanup: azcmagent disconnect, then delete the Arc machine resource.

demos.title: The AVD Hybrid extension on an Arc machine

followAlong.goal: Register an Arc-enabled Windows 11 machine as an AVD Hybrid session host.
needs: A standard host pool created without VMs and with a managed identity
Reader for that identity on the Arc resource group
An Arc-enabled, Entra-joined Windows 11 Enterprise VM
Az.DesktopVirtualization and Az.ConnectedMachine

steps.title: Generate a registration token
steps.instructions: Create a short-lived token; keep it in memory only.
steps.check: $token is populated.

steps.title: Install the extension
steps.instructions: Install the AVD Hybrid extension on the Arc machine with the token as a protected setting.
steps.check: The extension shows Succeeded.

steps.title: Wait for the host
steps.instructions: The host can take up to 15 minutes to become Available after the extension succeeds.
steps.check: The host shows Available.

troubleshooting: Host stays Unavailable: confirm Reader for the pool's managed identity on the Arc resource group and outbound access to the AVD service URLs.
cleanup: Remove the extension and the session host from the pool.

demos.title: The profile share, per-user containers and the settings that make them portable

followAlong.goal: Configure FSLogix profile and ODFC containers on an Azure Files share and confirm a container is created.
needs: A session host (Entra-joined)
A share with Entra Kerberos enabled (see the identity demo)
FSLogix installed on the host

steps.title: Apply the FSLogix settings
steps.instructions: Apply the repo's configuration profile (replace the share path with yours).
steps.check: Test-FslogixHostConfig reports the settings applied.

steps.title: Sign in once and check the container
steps.instructions: Sign in to the host as a test user, sign out, then list the share.
steps.check: A Profile VHDX (and ODFC VHDX) exists under the user's folder.

steps.title: Publish redirections.xml
steps.instructions: Publish the exclusion file to the share so every host uses the same one.
steps.check: redirections.xml is in the redirections folder of the share.

troubleshooting: Temporary profile on sign-in: check the share path, the user's role on the share and the ticket (klist).
cleanup: Delete the test user's folder from the share.

demos.title: One repo, one config, three realms

followAlong.goal: Preview a change to the AVD control plane without applying it.
needs: The repo
An existing control-plane deployment or a test resource group

steps.title: Run a what-if
steps.instructions: Change one parameter (for example the host pool session limit) and run what-if.
steps.command: az deployment group what-if -g <rg> --template-file automation/avd/control-plane/bicep/main.bicep --parameters <your parameter file>
steps.check: The output lists one modified property.

troubleshooting: What-if shows noise: some properties are service-computed; compare only the properties you changed.

demos.title: Crossing 1: three host pools, one workspace

followAlong.goal: Check your host pools are healthy before testing portability.
needs: Two host pools, one user group per pool

steps.title: Check host status
steps.instructions: List session hosts and sessions.
steps.command: Get-AzWvdHostPool -ResourceGroupName <rg> | ForEach-Object { Get-AzWvdSessionHost -ResourceGroupName <rg> -HostPoolName $_.Name | Select-Object Name, Status, Session }
steps.check: All hosts Available with no sessions.

demos.title: Crossing 2: the user is entitled to the right realm

followAlong.goal: Control which desktop a user sees with group membership.
needs: Two application groups, each assigned to a different Entra group
A test user

steps.title: Add the user to the first group
steps.instructions: Add the test user to the group assigned to the first application group.
steps.check: The user sees one desktop in Windows App.

steps.title: Move the user to the second group
steps.instructions: Remove from group A and add to group B; refresh the feed.
steps.command:
Remove-AzADGroupMember -GroupObjectId <group A id> -MemberUserPrincipalName <user>
Add-AzADGroupMember -TargetGroupObjectId <group B id> -MemberUserPrincipalName <user>
steps.check: After refresh the feed shows the second desktop only.

troubleshooting: Feed unchanged: allow a few minutes, then refresh or sign out and in of Windows App.

followAlong.goal: Prove a profile follows a user across two host pools.
needs: Two host pools using the same FSLogix share and configuration
A test user entitled to both pools (one at a time)

steps.title: Create state in the profile
steps.instructions: Sign in to pool 1, create a file on the desktop and change a setting such as the wallpaper.
steps.check: File and setting present.

steps.title: Sign out and confirm the container released
steps.instructions: Sign out; confirm no open handle on the container before signing in elsewhere.
steps.check: The container shows a recent last write and no open handles.

steps.title: Sign in to pool 2
steps.instructions: Sign in to the second pool.
steps.check: The hostname belongs to pool 2 and the file and setting are present.

troubleshooting: File missing: confirm OneDrive Known Folder Move is off so you are testing FSLogix, and that both pools use the same share path.
cleanup: Delete the test file and restore the setting.

demos.title: Crossing 4: forced host failure on Hybrid

followAlong.goal: See what a host failure does to a session and what survives.
needs: A host pool with two Available hosts (VMs you can stop)
FSLogix profile on shared storage
A test user with a session

steps.title: Start a session and leave an unsaved document open
steps.instructions: Sign in and open a document without saving it.
steps.check: The session is on host 1.

steps.title: Stop host 1 hard
steps.instructions: Stop the VM without a graceful shutdown (for a Hyper-V VM: Stop-VM -TurnOff).
steps.check: The host shows Unavailable in the pool after a minute or two.

steps.title: Open a new session
steps.instructions: Reconnect from Windows App; the broker sends you to host 2.
steps.check: You are on host 2; your saved files and settings are present; the unsaved document is not.

steps.title: Restart host 1
steps.instructions: Start the VM; AVD does not do this for you in a Hybrid realm.
steps.check: The host returns to Available.

troubleshooting: Profile will not attach: a stale handle on the container; wait for the SMB session to expire or close the handle on the share.

followAlong.goal: Query all your hosts from one workspace.
needs: Azure Monitor Agent on hosts reporting to one workspace

steps.title: Run a heartbeat query
steps.instructions: Show the last heartbeat per host.
steps.command: Heartbeat | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | summarize last = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | order by Computer asc
steps.check: Every host you expect, with a recent last heartbeat.

troubleshooting: Missing host: check the Azure Monitor Agent and the DCR association.
